pageCache.text:
Residential, therapeutic care and support • Education Semi - independent living for care leavers
Cameron & Co
was born from a desire to provide the best possible care and support to vulnerable young people. Founded in 2017 by our Director, Camilla McInnes, who was working with looked after children as a therapist and was passionate about helping young people faced with adversity
Cameron & Co was created with a clear purpose: to provide homes and education where young people feel safe, understood, and genuinely cared for.
Love, Care and Consistency underpins how we work. Adults build meaningful relationships with young people, respond in a calm and consistent way, and provide clear boundaries that support safety and stability. When young people are struggling, adults stay alongside them. This consistency over time helps young people to feel secure, build trust, and begin to move forward.
Many of the young people who come to us have experienced early adversity that can affect how they trust others, manage emotions, and engage with the world around them. We recognise this and respond in a way that is calm, predictable, and relational. Adults take time to understand each young person and place them at the centre of everything we do, ensuring care and support is shaped around their individual needs.
Our journey began with the opening of The Beech House, a residential children’s home for young people aged 10 to 17. The home offers a safe, stable, and caring environment where young people can begin to build trust, develop confidence, and feel part of a home. Adults take the time to understand each young person and support them day to day, providing the consistency and care needed for them to make meaningful progress from where they started.
As our understanding of young people’s needs developed, we opened The Beech House School in 2018. The school provides structure, routine, and a sense of achievement, allowing young people to re-engage with education in a way that feels manageable. Adults work alongside them to build confidence, recognise effort, and celebrate progress.
We have continued to grow our residential provision in a way that reflects the needs of young people. Cherry Blossom was developed as a smaller home, offering a more contained and responsive environment for young people who benefit from higher levels of individual support. We are also preparing to open Acacia Cottage in summer 2026, which will further strengthen our ability to provide safe, loving, and consistent care.
Looking ahead, we are developing a new school provision, with a planned opening in September 2027. This will allow us to extend our educational offer and support more children and young people in an environment that is caring, consistent, and focused on positive outcomes.
Across all of our homes and our school, young people experience adults who are present, consistent, and committed. We believe that when young people are met with genuine love, care, clear boundaries, and consistent relationships they can rely on, they are better able to understand themselves, trust others, and move forward positively.
The Beech House
The Beech House is a therapeutic children’s home in Surrey, offering care for up to five young people aged 10–17.
Cherry Blossom
Cherry Blossom is a small, therapeutic children’s home near Farnham in Surrey, offering care for up to two young people aged 10–17.
Acacia Cottage
Acacia is a three-bed therapeutic children’s home in Surrey, providing care for up to three young people aged 10–17.

SEMH Teacher – The Beech House School
SEMH Secondary Teacher
The Beech House School
Pay: £35,000.00-£50,000.00 per year
Are you driven by the belief that education can be a force for healing, identity-building, and change? Do you thrive in a values-led environment where relationships, creativity, and compassion are at the heart of everything? If so, The Beech House School may be your next home.
The Beech House School is part of a deeply human, therapeutically informed journey — one that began with the desire to help young people build safe, meaningful attachments and process complex life experiences. Cameron & Cooper Limited was founded by a therapist passionate about the power of PACE, attachment, and relationship, our community now includes residential childrens homes, supported accommodation for 18-25’s, and a specialist SEMH school — all working together to provide safety, belonging, and opportunity.
This is more than a job. It’s a chance to help young people with complex stories to reconnect with learning, with others, and with themselves. You’ll be part of a close-knit, high-trust team delivering small-group, trauma-informed education — where practical creativity, therapeutic pedagogy, and personal development sit side by side. Whether you’re teaching English or leading outdoor learning, co-regulating in a nurture space or coaching colleagues on curriculum, your work will matter here. Deeply.
Rooted in Love, Care, and Consistency, we are unapologetically ambitious for our pupils — and for the adults who work alongside them. If you’re ready to lead with heart, teach with purpose, and grow within a truly therapeutic setting, we’d love to hear from you.
About The Beech House School
The Beech House School is a newly redeveloped Independent Specialist SEMH school for looked-after children aged 11–18. We are growing steadily from an initial cohort of 12–15 pupils, and are proud to be rated Good by Ofsted, with three consecutive Good inspections since opening.
Every interaction in our school is a chance to build safety, trust, and growth.
Our environment — including our beautifully renovated Grade II Listed building — is purposefully shaped to support regulation and connection. We’re developing an in-house therapeutic model in collaboration with care and clinical teams, with a full-time Education Therapist embedded in our education staff.
